title: Fractional Optimal Control For Infinite Variables Parabolic SystemsWith Time Lags Given In Integral Form
content:
In this paper, the fractional optimal control problem for
distributed parabolic systems involving constant lags in the
integral form both in the state equations and in the boundary
condition is considered. The fractional time derivative is
considered in a Caputo sense. The system contains model operator of
second order with infinite number of variables. We first study the
existence and the uniqueness of the solution of the fractional
differential system with time delay in a Hilbert space. Then we show
that the considered optimal control problem has a unique solution.
The performance index of a (FOCP) is considered as a function of
both state and control variables, and the dynamic constraints are
expressed by a Partial Fractional Differential Equation (PFDE). The
time horizon is fixed. Finally, we impose some constraints on the
boundary control. Interpreting the Euler-–Lagrange first-order
optimality condition with an adjoint problem defined by means of
right fractional Caputo derivative, we obtain an optimality system
for the fractional optimal control. Some specific properties of the
optimal control are discussed. Some examples are analyzed in
details.
